spec.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
spec.conclusion: U=V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K is nonzero, and every K-linear subspace W⊂U invariant under the induced x,y,h actions equals zero or U; equivalently it is irreducible for the prescribed L_K action. This holds for every original choice of p,K,λ,V,x,y,h,v,M satisfying H001–H006, including λ=0 and p=2, with no algebraic-closure hypothesis on K.

hypotheses.statement: V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1.
The complex-linear Chevalley operators satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h; v≠0, xv=0, hv=λv.

M⊂V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z (equivalently under every X_r,Y_r for r≥0). M is not assumed minimal.

definitions.definition: ell=Int.toNat(λ). When λ≥0 its integer image is λ; this equality is used only with H003.
I={0,...,ell}, equivalently Fin(n), of cardinal n. Index arithmetic in factorials and binomials is natural arithmetic; weights ell−2i are integer expressions, then cast to the scalar field.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For r∈ℕ, X_r=(r! as a complex scalar)^{-1} x^r. Products of endomorphisms mean composition, rightmost factor first.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For r∈ℕ, Y_r=(r! as a complex scalar)^{-1} y^r.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the complex universal enveloping algebra of sl₂
definitions.definition: U_Z is the ℤ-subalgebra generated by x^r/r! and y^r/r! for all natural r, acting on V through the given representation; these actions are X_r and Y_r.
U=V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K. K acts on the K factor. For any ℤ-endomorphism f of M its induced operator on U sends m⊗c to f(m)⊗c.

definitions.type: K-Lie algebra with its induced action on U
definitions.definition: L_K=L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K in the original Chevalley construction. Its action on U is induced from the lattice restrictions of x,y,h and extended K-linearly; the integral Chevalley lattice is used also in characteristic 2.
For i∈I define e_i=Y_i v=y^i v/i!. This definition does not assert that e is a basis.
For j∈I, c_j=binom(ell,j). A bar over any integer or natural coefficient below means its image under ℤ→K.
C=∏_{j∈I} c_j; the empty product is 1.
For i∈I, d_i=∏_{j∈I,j≠i} c_j, with empty product 1.
Q=Y_ell X_ell. This is the operator called P in basis-proof.md; Q avoids conflict with the target ID P.

a_ij is the restriction of A_ij to M. H006 ensures that each divided-power factor preserves M and thus that this restriction exists. Superscript M on X,Y,x,y,h denotes their lattice restriction; h^M exists since h=xy−yx.
T=K⊗_ℤ M, with scalar action on the K factor.

definitions.type: scalar-extension operation on ℤ-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For f∈End_ℤ(M), hat(f)=LinearMap.baseChange K f∈End_K(T), the canonical scalar extension. Its pure-tensor formula is the assertion M007. Write x̂=hat(x^M), ŷ=hat(y^M), ĥ=hat(h^M), X̂_r=hat(X_r^M), Ŷ_r=hat(Y_r^M) when the restrictions exist.
F_ij=(c_j as a scalar in K)^{-1} hat(a_ij). Inversion uses the field's total inverse; nonzeroness of c_j is proved in N003, not assumed here.

For i∈I, x e_0=0; x e_i=(ell−i+1)e_{i−1} for 1≤i≤ell; y e_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<ell; y e_ell=0; h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i. For every natural r and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(ell−i+r,r)e_{i−r} if r≤i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤ell and is zero otherwise.

For each j∈I, c_j>0 and c_j j!(ell−j)!=ell!, and binom(ell,ell−j)=c_j. On the complex basis e, Q e_ell=e_ell and Q e_k=0 for k<ell. For every i,j,k∈I, A_ij e_k=c_j e_i if k=j and is zero otherwise. Every A_ij preserves M and its restriction is a_ij. The following are equalities of ℤ-endomorphisms of M: for all i,j,k,l∈I, a_ij a_kl=c_j a_il if j=k, and zero otherwise; ∑_{i∈I} d_i a_ii=C Id_M; and C=c_i d_i for each i∈I. For every natural r, r! X_r^M=(x^M)^r and r! Y_r^M=(y^M)^r. The restrictions of x,y,h exist and h^M=x^M y^M−y^M x^M.

ell has integer image λ and ell<p; n=ell+1>0. T is a nonzero finite-dimensional K-vector space with dimension n. For every natural r≤ell, (r! as a scalar in K)≠0. Each c_j (j∈I) and C has nonzero image in K. The endomorphisms F of T satisfy, for all i,j,k,l∈I, F_ij F_kl=F_il when j=k and are zero otherwise, and ∑_{i∈I} F_ii=Id_T. For r≤ell, X̂_r=(r! as a scalar in K)^{-1}x̂^r and Ŷ_r=(r! as a scalar in K)^{-1}ŷ^r; ĥ=x̂ŷ−ŷx̂.

U=M⊗_ℤ K is a nonzero finite-dimensional K-vector space of dimension n=ell+1>0. There exists a family G:I×I→End_K(U) such that G_ij G_kl=G_il if j=k and zero otherwise for all i,j,k,l∈I, and ∑_{i∈I}G_ii=Id_U. Every K-linear subspace W⊂U invariant under the original induced x,y actions is invariant under all G_ij. The induced h action is the commutator of the induced x and y actions. The representation is precisely the original L_K action, also in characteristic 2.

For every field F0, natural n0>0, finite-dimensional F0-vector space U0 with dimension n0, and family G0 of F0-linear endomorphisms indexed by 0≤i,j<n0, suppose G0_ij G0_kl=G0_il if j=k and zero otherwise and ∑_{0≤i<n0}G0_ii=Id_U0. Then every F0-linear subspace W0 of U0 invariant under all G0_ij equals zero or U0.

locals.type: family of vectors indexed by natural numbers
locals.declaration: Define t_r=y^r v for every natural r.
For the induction step fix an arbitrary natural r.
Let q_i be the coordinates of t_{ell+1} in the proved basis e.

argument.text:
H003 gives ell=λ as integers, hence n=ell+1>0; we use ell for the nonnegative highest weight. Define t_r=y^r v. H005 gives t_0=v, h t_0=ell t_0 and x t_0=0. Induct on a natural r. Temporarily assume L1: h t_r=(ell−2r)t_r and, for r≥1, x t_r=r(ell−r+1)t_{r−1}, with x t_0=0 separately. From hy=yh−2y one gets h t_{r+1}=(ell−2r−2)t_{r+1}. From xy=yx+h, for r≥1,
x t_{r+1}=y x t_r+h t_r=[r(ell−r+1)+ell−2r]t_r=(r+1)(ell−r)t_r.
For r=0 the same result is x y v=y x v+h v=ell v. This proves the step and discharges L1. Natural induction proves the stated h and x formulas for every r; scalar subtractions here are in ℤ and then ℂ.

produces.statement: ell=λ as integers and n>0; for every r∈ℕ, h t_r=(ell−2r)t_r, x t_0=0, and x t_r=r(ell−r+1)t_{r−1} when r≥1.

argument.text:
For each i∈I, iterate F001 to obtain
x^i t_i=[∏_{s=1}^i s(ell−s+1)]v=i!·[ell(ell−1)⋯(ell−i+1)]v.
Every factor is a positive integer for 1≤s≤i≤ell, so its complex image is nonzero; the empty product for i=0 is 1. H005 supplies v≠0. Hence t_i≠0. Since i!≠0 in ℂ, e_i=t_i/i!≠0, and F001 gives h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i. For i,j∈I, equality of these complex weights forces 2(i−j)=0 and hence i=j in characteristic zero.

produces.statement: For all i∈I, e_i≠0 and h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i; the function i↦(ell−2i)∈ℂ on I is injective.

argument.text: Apply M001 to the ℂ-vector space V, endomorphism h, eigenvalue function i↦ell−2i on I, and family e. A complex vector space is torsion-free over the integral domain ℂ: a nonzero scalar has an inverse, so a z=0 forces z=0. F002 supplies injectivity and all nonzero eigenvector equations. Thus e is complex-linearly independent.

The given complex dimension in H004 is λ+1=ell+1=n by F001. The module is finite-dimensional by that given dimension. The finite set I has n elements. Apply M002 to F003 and |I|=dim_ℂ V to obtain span_ℂ(e)=V. Together with independence, this says e is a complex basis.

produces.statement: e is a complex basis of V indexed by I.

argument.text: F001 gives h t_{ell+1}=(−ell−2)t_{ell+1}. Using F004, define its unique coordinates q_i by t_{ell+1}=∑_{i∈I}q_i e_i. The eigenvector equation and the basis equations give q_i[(ell−2i)−(−ell−2)]=0 for every i. The bracket is 2(ell+1−i), a nonzero complex scalar since i≤ell. Consequently every q_i=0, and t_{ell+1}=0. Since t_{r+1}=y t_r, induction gives t_r=0 for all r>ell.

produces.statement: t_{ell+1}=0 and t_r=0 for all natural r>ell.

argument.text: Divide the F001 formulas by i!, using the nonzero complex factorials, and use F005. This gives x e_0=0, x e_i=(ell−i+1)e_{i−1} for 1≤i≤ell; y e_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<ell and y e_ell=0; h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i. Iterating the x formula r times for r≤i accumulates (ell−i+1)⋯(ell−i+r)=(ell−i+r)!/(ell−i)!. Divide by r! in ℂ, and apply M005 with nb=ell−i+r,kb=r to identify this as binom(ell−i+r,r). Iterating y for i+r≤ell accumulates (i+1)⋯(i+r)=(i+r)!/i!; M005 with nb=i+r,kb=r yields binom(i+r,r) after division by r!. Both bounds kb≤nb hold by natural addition. If r>i, the x iterate reaches e_0 and is then killed; if i+r>ell, the y iterate reaches e_ell and is then killed. The case r=0 gives identity, including all empty products. These are precisely the X,Y formulas in N001, together with the basis F004 and conversion F001.

applications.bindings: Rb=ℂ, Vb=V, Jb=I, fb=h, μb(i)=ell−2i, zb=e.
hypothesis_checks: ℂ is an integral domain; the scalar inverse argument in S003 proves torsion-freeness of V.
F002 proves injectivity over ℂ.
F002 proves nonzero eigenvectors and their h equations.
H004 gives finite-dimensionality and I=Fin(n) is finite.
F003 proves independence.
H004 and F001 give dim V=ell+1=n=|I|.

applications.bindings: For the raising coefficient use nb=ell−i+r,kb=r for r≤i; for lowering use nb=i+r,kb=r; i∈I and r natural in the indicated ranges.
hypothesis_checks: r≤ell−i+r and r≤i+r follow by addition of nonnegative natural numbers.

locals.declaration: Using the basis in N001, define E_ij to send e_j to e_i and every e_k with k≠j to zero.

argument.text: For every j∈I apply M005 to nb=ell,kb=j, obtaining c_j j!(ell−j)!=ell!. Since ell!>0 and both factorials are positive integers, c_j>0. Apply M005 also to kb=ell−j. The two factorial products j!(ell−j)! and (ell−j)!j! coincide; cancel their positive value to get binom(ell,ell−j)=binom(ell,j)=c_j.

produces.statement: For every j∈I, c_j>0, c_j j!(ell−j)!=ell!, and binom(ell,ell−j)=c_j.

argument.text: Using the basis e from N001 define E_ij as stated. If k<ell, X_ell e_k=0; while X_ell e_ell=e_0 and Y_ell e_0=e_ell. Thus Q=Y_ell X_ell=E_{ell,ell}. N001 also gives X_{ell−i}e_ell=e_i, its coefficient being binom(ell−i,ell−i)=1. For i,j,k∈I, compute Q Y_{ell−j}e_k. If k<j, this is killed by Q because the lowered index k+ell−j is below ell; if k>j, the Y iterate is already zero past the end of the string. If k=j, it is binom(ell,ell−j)e_ell=c_j e_ell by F001. Therefore A_ij=X_{ell−i}QY_{ell−j}=c_j E_ij on the whole complex space, since equality on a basis implies equality of linear maps.

produces.statement: Q=E_{ell,ell} and, for all i,j∈I, A_ij=c_j E_ij as complex-linear maps of V.

argument.text: Evaluation on e shows E_ij E_kl=E_il if j=k and zero otherwise, and ∑_i E_ii=Id_V. Substitute F002: A_ij A_kl=c_j A_il if j=k and zero otherwise, since when j=k the product is c_j c_l E_il. Finite product decomposition gives C=c_i d_i for each i. Hence ∑_i d_i A_ii=∑_i C E_ii=C Id_V. By H006 every factor defining A_ij preserves M, so a_ij is its ℤ-linear restriction. For any vector of M the two sides of each integer identity have equal images in V; the inclusion M→V is injective, so the product and sum identities hold in End_ℤ(M). This restriction uses only integer coefficients, with no assertion that E preserves M and no rational scalar action on M.

produces.statement: Every A_ij preserves M, a_ij a_kl=c_j a_il for j=k and zero otherwise, C=c_i d_i, and ∑_{i∈I}d_i a_ii=C Id_M.

argument.text: For every natural r, definitions give r! X_r=x^r and r! Y_r=y^r in End_ℂ(V), since r! is nonzero in ℂ. H006 ensures all these maps preserve M, including X_1=x and Y_1=y. Restricting the equalities through the injective inclusion gives r! X_r^M=(x^M)^r and r! Y_r^M=(y^M)^r on M. H005 gives h=xy−yx, so h preserves M and h^M=x^M y^M−y^M x^M. With F001–F003 these prove all statements in N002.

applications.bindings: nb=ell, kb=j and kb=ell−j, for each j∈I.
hypothesis_checks: j≤ell by I, and ell−j≤ell by natural subtraction.

locals.type: ℤ-basis of M indexed by I

locals.type: K-basis of T indexed by I
locals.declaration: Define β=b.baseChange K, the canonical scalar-extended basis.
Fix any ℤ-linear endomorphism f of M.
Fix any ℤ-linear endomorphism g of M.
Fix an arbitrary integer z.
Fix an arbitrary scalar α∈K.
Fix an arbitrary m∈M.

argument.text: By H003, the integer image of ell is λ, and ell<p; n=ell+1>0. H006 supplies an integer basis of M whose images form a complex basis of V. H004 says the latter space has finite dimension λ+1=n. Thus that basis has exactly n members (the finite-dimensional basis cardinality property), and reindexing by I gives an I-indexed paired basis. In particular there exists such a ℤ-basis of M. No property of the divided-power coordinates e as lattice vectors is being used.

produces.statement:
ell=λ as integers, ell

0; there exists an I-indexed ℤ-basis b of M whose images form a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Choose b from F001. Let β=b.baseChange K, a K-basis of T. M003, with the canonical ℤ-algebra structure of K, identifies β_i=1⊗b_i for every i∈I. Apply M006 to this finite K-basis: dim_K T=|I|=n. It spans with finitely many members, so T is finite-dimensional. Since n>0, the index 0 belongs to I; β_0≠0, for a zero basis vector would contradict independence using coefficient 1≠0 in the field K. Therefore T is nonzero.

produces.statement: β is a K-basis of T, β_i=1⊗b_i for each i∈I, dim_K T=n, T is finite-dimensional and nonzero.

argument.text:
Fix arbitrary ℤ-endomorphisms f,g of M, z∈ℤ, α∈K and m∈M. Use M007 to obtain hat(f)(α⊗m)=α⊗f(m). Pure tensors span T: write m=∑_{i∈I} z_i b_i in the basis b and expand α⊗m=∑_i (z_i α)(1⊗b_i) by additivity and balance. Equivalently β in F002 spans. On an arbitrary pure tensor,
hat(f)hat(g)(α⊗m)=α⊗f(g(m)),
hat(f+g)(α⊗m)=α⊗(f(m)+g(m)),
hat(zf)(α⊗m)=α⊗(z f(m))=(zα)⊗f(m).
The same formula for the identity fixes every pure tensor. Equality on spanning pure tensors thus proves preservation of composition, addition, integer scalar multiplication and identity by hat. Finite sums and powers follow by induction. No injectivity or faithfulness of scalar extension is assumed.

produces.statement: For every f∈End_ℤ(M), hat(f)(α⊗m)=α⊗f(m) for all α∈K,m∈M. The operation hat preserves addition, integer scalar multiplication (cast into K), composition, identity, finite sums and powers.

argument.text:
For every natural r≤ell, F001 gives r<p. Apply M004 with Ab=K,pb=p,rb=r using H001,H002. The scalar r! is a unit, hence is nonzero in K; in particular ell!≠0. For each j∈I apply M005 with nb=ell,kb=j and cast the identity into K:
(c_j mod K)·(j! mod K)·((ell−j)! mod K)=(ell! mod K)≠0.
If c_j had zero image, the left side would vanish, a contradiction. Hence every c_j has nonzero image. Since K is a field, their finite product, the image of C, is nonzero.

produces.statement: For all natural r≤ell, (r! mod K)≠0; for every j∈I, (c_j mod K)≠0, and (C mod K)≠0.

argument.text:
Apply F003 to the integer identities in N002. The extended product relation is hat(a_ij)hat(a_kl)=(c_j mod K)hat(a_il) for j=k, and zero otherwise. By definition F_ij=(c_j mod K)^{-1}hat(a_ij). For j≠k the product F_ij F_kl is zero. For j=k it is
(c_j mod K)^{-1}(c_l mod K)^{-1}(c_j mod K)hat(a_il)=(c_l mod K)^{-1}hat(a_il)=F_il,
using F004 for cancellation. Extend ∑_i d_i a_ii=C Id_M to T. Since C=c_i d_i and c_i,C have nonzero images, (C mod K)^{-1}(d_i mod K)=(c_i mod K)^{-1}. Multiplying the extended sum by (C mod K)^{-1} gives ∑_i F_ii=Id_T. This proves genuine matrix units without reducing a complex coordinate basis.

produces.statement: For all i,j,k,l∈I, F_ij F_kl=F_il if j=k and zero otherwise; ∑_{i∈I}F_ii=Id_T.

argument.text: Extend the factorial identities from N002 using F003. For each natural r≤ell this gives (r! mod K)X̂_r=x̂^r and (r! mod K)Ŷ_r=ŷ^r. Invert the nonzero factorials from F004 to obtain X̂_r=(r! mod K)^{-1}x̂^r and Ŷ_r=(r! mod K)^{-1}ŷ^r. Extending h^M=x^M y^M−y^M x^M gives ĥ=x̂ŷ−ŷx̂. F001,F002,F004,F005 and these identities give every clause of N003; none depends on the particular paired basis b chosen for the dimension argument.

applications.bindings: Rb=ℤ, Sb=K with its canonical ℤ-algebra structure, Vb=M, Jb=I, bb=b, for every i∈I.
hypothesis_checks: ℤ is a commutative ring, K is a field and hence an ℤ-algebra semiring, M is an additive subgroup and thus a ℤ-module.
F001 supplies b, chosen in S002, as an I-indexed basis; the equation is applied to every index of I.
A field satisfies the strong rank condition: finite free spaces have invariant basis size, the usual finite linear-algebra dimension property.
I=Fin(n) is finite; β is the scalar-extended basis, with its coordinates identified by M003 in S002.

applications.bindings: Rb=ℤ, Ab=K, Vb=Wb=M, fb=f, cb=α, mb=m; also the same substitution for g,f+g,zf,fg and the identity.
hypothesis_checks: ℤ is commutative and K has its canonical ℤ-algebra structure.
M is an additive abelian group and a ℤ-module by its given subgroup structure.
f,g are arbitrary ℤ-endomorphisms, so all displayed sums, compositions and scalar multiples are ℤ-linear; α∈K,m∈M are arbitrary.

applications.bindings: Ab=K as a ring, pb=p, rb=r for every r≤ell.
hypothesis_checks: H001 gives primality of p.
H002 gives characteristic p on K; F001 gives r≤ell<p, so the reverse implication of M004 applies.

hypothesis_checks: j≤ell because j∈I.

locals.declaration: Construct the balanced tensor map s(m⊗α)=α⊗m.
Construct the balanced tensor map t(α⊗m)=m⊗α.
Fix any K-subspace W of T.
Define G_ij=t F_ij s for all i,j∈I.

argument.text: Construct s:U→T by m⊗α↦α⊗m and t:T→U by α⊗m↦m⊗α. Each assignment is additive in each argument. For z∈ℤ, (zm)⊗α=m⊗(zα) is sent to α⊗(zm)=(zα)⊗m, exactly the balance relation in T; the reverse check is identical. The tensor universal property therefore gives additive maps, which are K-linear for the scalar action on the K factor. Both composites fix every pure tensor, hence are identities since pure tensors generate the tensor spaces. For any ℤ-endomorphism f of M, s(f(m)⊗α)=α⊗f(m)=hat(f)(s(m⊗α)) by N003. Thus s,t are inverse K-linear maps intertwining every induced lattice operator.

produces.statement: s:U→T and t:T→U are inverse K-linear maps. For every f∈End_ℤ(M), s intertwines the induced f action on U with hat(f) on T.

argument.text: Fix any K-subspace W of T and assume L1: W is invariant under x̂ and ŷ. The identity preserves W. Inductively, if the r-th power of either operator preserves W, applying that operator once more shows its (r+1)-st power preserves W. Thus all their natural powers preserve W. By N003 and closure under K-scalar multiplication, W is invariant under X̂_r,Ŷ_r for every r≤ell. N002 expresses a_ij as the composition of the four restrictions X_{ell−i},Y_ell,X_ell,Y_{ell−j}. Scalar extension preserves this composition by N003. All four indices lie between 0 and ell, so W is invariant under hat(a_ij), then under its scalar multiple F_ij. Discharge L1 and quantify over W: every x̂,ŷ-invariant subspace of T is invariant under every F_ij.

produces.statement: For every K-subspace W of T, if W is invariant under x̂ and ŷ, it is invariant under all F_ij, i,j∈I.

argument.text: Define G_ij=t F_ij s. Because st=Id_T and ts=Id_U from F001, multiplication and the sum relation in N003 transport to G_ij G_kl=G_il for j=k and zero otherwise, and ∑_i G_ii=Id_U. The same K-linear equivalence transports nonzeroness, finite-dimensionality and dim T=n from N003 to U. For any K-subspace of U invariant under its original induced x,y operators, its image under s is invariant under x̂,ŷ by F001; F002 makes that image invariant under every F_ij. Applying t proves the original subspace invariant under every G_ij. The commutator identity for ĥ in N003 and the intertwinings show that the transported h is exactly the original induced h. H006 and N002 ensure all lattice restrictions exist, so D008 gives precisely the prescribed L_K action. We have thus constructed the family required in N004 for the original U=M⊗_ℤ K.

Fix an arbitrary natural n0.
Fix an arbitrary F0-vector space U0.

locals.declaration: Fix a family G0 of endomorphisms with the indicated indices.
Fix an arbitrary subspace W0 of U0.
Choose w∈W0 with w≠0 using F001.
Choose j with G0_jj w≠0 using F002.
Define u=G0_jj w.
Define uvec_i=G0_ij u for every i∈Fin(n0).
For the independence proof fix arbitrary coefficients coef_i∈F0.
Fix an arbitrary k∈Fin(n0) in the coefficient argument.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary F0,n0,U0,G0,W0 as declared. Assume L1: n0>0, U0 is finite-dimensional over F0 with dimension n0, G0_ij G0_kl=G0_il when j=k and zero otherwise, ∑_i G0_ii=Id_U0, and W0 is invariant under every G0_ij. If W0=0, the required zero-or-whole alternative already holds. In the other branch assume L2: W0≠0. Then there exists w∈W0 with w≠0, since otherwise every member would be zero and W0 would be the zero subspace.
Choose w∈W0 with w≠0 from F001. Evaluating ∑_j G0_jj=Id_U0 at w yields ∑_j G0_jj w=w. If every term were zero, the sum would be zero, contradicting w≠0. Thus there exists j∈Fin(n0) with G0_jj w≠0.

produces.statement: There exists j∈Fin(n0) such that G0_jj w≠0.

argument.text: Choose j from F002, and put u=G0_jj w. Invariance gives u∈W0, and u≠0. The multiplication law gives G0_jj u=u by idempotence. Define uvec_i=G0_ij u for every i∈Fin(n0); all uvec_i belong to W0. To prove independence fix arbitrary coefficients coef and assume L3: ∑_i coef_i uvec_i=0. For arbitrary k∈Fin(n0), apply G0_jk. Its product with G0_ij is zero when k≠i, and is G0_jj when k=i. Thus G0_jk uvec_i=0 for i≠k, while G0_jk uvec_k=G0_jj u=u. Linearity reduces the relation to coef_k u=0. Since u≠0 over the field F0, coef_k=0: if nonzero, multiplication by its inverse would force u=0. Every coefficient vanishes. Discharge L3; this proves that uvec is linearly independent.

produces.statement: uvec:Fin(n0)→U0 is F0-linearly independent, and every uvec_i lies in W0.

argument.text: Apply M002 to Fb=F0,Vb=U0,Jb=Fin(n0),zb=uvec. F003 gives independence; L1 gives finite-dimensionality and |Fin(n0)|=n0=dim_F0 U0. The family spans U0. Since W0 contains its members by F003 and is a subspace, W0 contains their span, hence W0=U0 in the L2 branch. Discharge L2 by combining this branch with the already settled W0=0 branch; the dichotomy holds under L1. Discharge L1 into the quantified implication, and universally quantify the arbitrary data. This is N005, for any field, without an algebraic-closure condition.

hypothesis_checks: L1 gives finite-dimensionality; Fin(n0) is finite.
F003 proves independence.
L1 gives dim_F0 U0=n0, and |Fin(n0)|=n0.

locals.declaration: Choose the matrix-unit family G_U supplied by N004, including its invariance property.
Fix any K-linear subspace W of U.

argument.text: N004 supplies a nonzero finite-dimensional U of dimension n>0 and an I-indexed matrix-unit family; choose that family as G_U with its full asserted invariance property. Here I=Fin(n). These are the required hypotheses for the universal lemma N005 on the original tensor module U.

Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂U, and assume L1: W is invariant under the original induced x,y,h. Its invariance under x,y alone implies invariance under all G_U, by N004. Instantiate N005 with F0=K,n0=n,U0=U,G0=G_U,W0=W. S001 gives the dimension and matrix-unit hypotheses, so W=0 or W=U. Discharge L1 and quantify over W. Together with nonzeroness from N004 this proves the requested irreducibility. H006 ensures the lattice actions in L_K are defined; invariance under its generators is equivalent to invariance under their K-linear combinations, since W is a K-subspace.

All data remain arbitrary under the original hypotheses. H003 includes λ=0 and p=2; it imposes no algebraic-closure condition on K. The nonnegative integer conversion gives ell=0 when λ=0, so n=1 and N004 yields a nonzero one-dimensional module. When p=2 the permitted λ are 0 and 1, and N004 and N005 apply to both, with no distinct-weight condition in characteristic p. Hence neither boundary case is excluded by any step of this final implication.
